scenes.say: DNA has two strands. Across the strands, adenine pairs with thymine and guanine pairs with cytosine.

X-linked alleles lie on the X chromosome. For these genes the Y chromosome does not carry a matching allele. An XY person can express an X-linked recessive trait with one altered allele. If the mother carries colour blindness and the father is affected, half of the children are expected to be affected.
During conjugation, two compatible Paramecium cells temporarily join and exchange micronuclear genetic material. This changes their genetic combinations.

JAMB asks which DNA bases pair, why X-linked haemophilia can show with one altered allele in an XY person, and which protist conjugates. Blue arrows show exchange of nuclear material between the cells.

quickCheck.prompt: Which base in DNA pairs with adenine?
quickCheck.feedback: Adenine pairs with thymine. Guanine pairs with cytosine.
